stories.title: ELSA3D: Elastic Semantic Anchoring for Unified 3D Understanding and Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: ELSA3D introduces a novel approach to unify 3D understanding and generation within a single foundation model.
It addresses the limitation of existing text-3D methods that flatten language and 3D tokens, losing structural and geometric detail.
The core innovation is 'elastic semantic anchoring,' which structures language and geometry separately for better representation.

stories.title: DepthWeave-KV: Token-Adaptive Cross-Layer Residual Factorization for Long-Context KV Cache Compression
stories.author: Jesus Olivera
bullet_points: Addresses the memory bottleneck in long-context language model inference caused by large Key-Value (KV) caches.
Introduces DepthWeave-KV, a novel token-adaptive cache compression method.
Achieves compression by factorizing key and value states across transformer layers using shared low-rank channel bases.

stories.title: FreqDepthKV: Frequency-Guided Depth Sharing for Robust KV Cache Compression in Long-Context LLM Inference
stories.author: Jesús Olivera
bullet_points: Addresses the critical memory and bandwidth bottleneck of KV caches in long-context LLM inference.
Introduces FreqDepthKV, a novel compression method that factorizes KV states into shared low-frequency components and sparse high-frequency residuals.
Uses a lightweight online probe to dynamically assign attention heads to shared, residual, or exact cache representations for efficient inference.

stories.title: The Key to Going Linear: Analysis-Driven Transformer Linearization
stories.author: Babak Ehteshami Bejnordi
bullet_points: Addresses the quadratic computational bottleneck of causal self-attention in long-context transformers.
Proposes an analysis-driven approach to transformer linearization, focusing on state update design.
Identifies that softmax relies on key-dependent, rank-1 orthogonal projections, offering insights into efficient attention mechanisms.

stories.title: PALS: Percentile-Aware Layerwise Sparsity for LLM Pruning
stories.author: Alexey Shvets
bullet_points: PALS introduces Percentile-Aware Layerwise Sparsity to improve LLM pruning efficiency.
It dynamically adjusts sparsity per layer based on activation magnitudes, unlike uniform methods.
PALS significantly outperforms uniform pruning (Wanda) on LLaMA-2-7B, achieving lower perplexity.

stories.title: Google updates Android Bench with new LLMs, but Gemini still lags behind
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam

stories.title: Two teens learn the hard way not to do toy gun drive-bys from a Waymo
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin

stories.title: The Large Cancer Assistant (LCA): A Model-Agnostic Orchestration Framework for Scalable Clinical Decision Support in Oncology
stories.author: Basarab Matei
bullet_points: Introduces the Large Cancer Assistant (LCA), a new orchestration framework for clinical decision support in oncology.
Addresses the limitation of monolithic deep learning models by decoupling data ingestion, clinical routing, and AI inference.
The LCA is designed to be model-agnostic, promoting scalability across various multimodal AI models.

stories.title: RSF-GLLM: Bridging the Semantic Gap in Multi-Hop Knowledge Graph QA via Recurrent Soft-Flow and Decoupled LLM Generation
stories.author: Ananth Muppidi
bullet_points: Introduces RSF-GLLM to solve the semantic gap in Multi-Hop Knowledge Graph Question Answering (QA).
Addresses the issue of non-differentiability in traditional retrieve-then-read pipelines.
Utilizes a Recurrent Soft-Flow (RSF) module with a GRU-guided query updater to enable continuous graph reasoning.

stories.title: Bridging Physical Reasoning and Task Generalization via Visual Action Outcome Reasoning Alignment
stories.author: Yu-Chiang Frank Wang
bullet_points: The research addresses a key limitation in Vision-Language Models (VLMs): poor generalization in interactive physical reasoning.
It tackles two specific failure modes: hallucinated reasoning that violates physics and misalignment between model reasoning and actual actions.
The proposed solution, VAORA, introduces a novel reward design to align visual reasoning with predicted action outcomes.

stories.title: Industry Classification of GitHub Repositories Using the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS)
stories.author: Alexander Quispe
bullet_points: Addresses the lack of standardized industry classification for GitHub repositories, a gap hindering innovation geography studies.
Introduces NAICS-GH, a new corpus mapping 6,588 GitHub repositories to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS).
The dataset covers repositories from the United States, the European Union, and Australia, enabling cross-regional analysis of open-source production.

stories.title: Co-LMLM: Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Models
stories.author: Yoav Artzi
bullet_points: Introduces Co-LMLM, a Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Model paradigm.
LMLMs externalize factual knowledge to a Knowledge Base (KB) instead of memorizing it in weights.
The new model allows for enhanced knowledge control capabilities beyond conventional LLMs by pairing continuous keys with textual knowledge.

stories.title: Selective Timestep Weighting and Advantage-Based Replay for Sample-Efficient Diffusion RLHF
stories.author: Soumik Mukhopadhyay
bullet_points: Addresses the sample inefficiency of applying Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) to diffusion models.
Proposes two new strategies: Selective Timestep Weighting and Advantage-Based Replay.
Aims to make diffusion RLHF more practical by reducing the reliance on large amounts of human or reward model evaluations.

stories.title: Agon: Competitive Cross-Model RL with Implicit Rival Grading of Reasoning
stories.author: Vladislav Beliaev
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in current RL-based reasoning models where only the final answer is graded, leading to verbose but not necessarily better reasoning.
Introduces 'Agon,' a novel framework where two competing models grade each other's solutions to a problem.
The competitive grading mechanism forces models to improve the quality of their reasoning trace, not just the final output.

stories.title: ECGLight: Compute-Light Framework For Paper ECG Digitization and Myocardial Infarction Screening
stories.author: Diego Paez-Granados
bullet_points: Introduces ECGLight, a compute-light framework designed for digitizing paper ECGs.
Addresses the challenge of analyzing physical ECGs in remote clinics lacking high computational power or internet access.
Aims to enable AI-based decision support for cardiovascular disease screening using legacy paper records.

stories.title: How Data Shapes RoPE Frequency Usage: From Positional Scale Matching to Length Generalization
stories.author: Ali Jadbabaie
bullet_points: The paper investigates the non-uniform usage of Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) in trained transformer models.
It proposes a data-centered explanation, suggesting RoPE frequencies are selected to match the relative-distance structure present in the training data.
The research formalizes a 'field-resolution tradeoff' related to the dependency profile width ($W$) induced by the data.

stories.title: Max Out GRPO Signal: Adaptive Trace Prefix Control for Hard Reasoning Problems
stories.author: Vladislav Beliaev
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) where hard examples fail to contribute gradients when no rollout succeeds.
The proposed method, AdaPrefix-GRPO, uses an adaptive trace prefix control mechanism to manage problem difficulty during training.
This technique treats prefix length as a continuous feedback-controlled knob, allowing the model to dynamically adjust the difficulty of challenging reasoning problems.

stories.title: Co-LMLM: Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Models
stories.author: Yoav Artzi
bullet_points: Introduces Co-LMLM, a Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Model.
LMLMs externalize factual knowledge to a Knowledge Base (KB) instead of memorizing it in weights.
The CO-LMLM paradigm offers enhanced knowledge control capabilities over conventional LLMs.

stories.title: From Noisy Traces to Root Causes: Structural Trajectory Analysis and Causal Extraction for Agent Optimization
stories.author: Yuqing Yang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of optimizing long-horizon AI agents that use LLMs for self-reflection and failure diagnosis.
Directly using large, noisy, and heterogeneous execution traces for optimization is inefficient and risks overfitting.
The proposed solution involves Structural Trajectory Analysis and Causal Extraction to move from noisy traces to identifying root causes for better agent policy improvement.

stories.title: Agon: Competitive Cross-Model RL with Implicit Rival Grading of Reasoning
stories.author: Vladislav Beliaev
bullet_points: Introduces 'Agon,' a novel approach to training reasoning models using competitive cross-model reinforcement learning.
Addresses a limitation in current RL-based reasoning models where only the final answer is graded, leading to verbose but not necessarily better reasoning.
Agon functions by having two competing models grade each other's solutions in an alternating drafting/review process.

stories.title: Does Bielik Know What It Doesn't Know? Activation Dispersion Separates Entity Familiarity from Factual Reliability Across Model Scale
stories.author: Grzegorz Brzezinka
bullet_points: The research investigates whether LLM internal activations can predict an entity's familiarity to the model before generation.
The study tests this hypothesis across four Polish Bielik models (1.5B-11B) using known, obscure, and fabricated entities.
The core finding suggests that activation dispersion may separate entity familiarity from the factual reliability of the model's output.

stories.title: DiaLLM: An Investigation into the Robustness-Generation Gap in English Dialect Adaptation
stories.author: Lu Yin
bullet_points: DiaLLM addresses the 'robustness-generation gap' in LLMs, where models understand dialects but fail to generate them.
The research involves continually pretraining three open-weight language model families on the International Corpus of English.
The methodology combines implicit/explicit post-training paradigms with various model alignment strategies for controlled comparison.

stories.title: RL Post-Training Builds Compositional Reasoning Strategies
stories.author: Andrew Saxe
bullet_points: The research investigates whether Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training enables models to compose primitive skills into higher-level reasoning strategies.
The study uses a fully observable rewrite-grammar environment, allowing for complete auditing of generated symbolic transformations.
A Transformer model was pretrained on primitive symbol-rewrite chains and then RL-tuned on a trace-based reasoning task with a binary reward.

stories.title: Future Confidence Distillation in Large Language Models
stories.author: Sahil Kale
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical need for reliable confidence estimation in Large Language Models (LLMs) for deployment in confidence-aware systems.
Existing methods often assess confidence only after the response is complete, failing to capture the dynamic nature of confidence during the generation process.
The paper proposes investigating confidence from a temporal perspective to improve the reliability assessment throughout the LLM answering process.
